turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Morning, come in, you two. What's been happening this side?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Um. My tummy, doctor. I don't know.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): Your tummy. Tell me what it feels like, in your own words.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): It gets big. After ice cream. And milk. Then I have to run.
[SEG0005] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She's shy, sorry. I'm her carer, I do the clinic runs. It's bloating and loose stools whenever there's dairy, and it's been months.
[SEG0006] person_1 (DOCTOR): Alright. Do you remember when it started, sweetheart?
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0008] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I'd put the bloating and the loose stools at about five months. Milk at breakfast sets her off, and ice cream is worse.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): How many times a day is she going, when it's loose?
[SEG0010] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Two or three. Not all day. If we skip the milk she's often fine. She won't count it herself.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any weight loss in that time?
[SEG0012] person_3 (CAREGIVER): No. No weight loss. Her school dress still fits, and she eats her pap and chicken. Traffic was hectic getting here, the robot on Main was out, but ja, weight's steady.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Did you manage to leave the dairy off for a proper stretch?
[SEG0014] person_3 (CAREGIVER): A week. No milk, no ice cream, no yoghurt. The bloating eased right off. Then Sunday a birthday milkshake and it came straight back.
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): It was lekker. Then my tummy was sore. I don't know.
[SEG0016] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any blood in the stool? Or stools that look black?
[SEG0017] person_3 (CAREGIVER): No blood, and nothing black. Just loose, and she gets urgent.
[SEG0018] person_1 (DOCTOR): Has she had a fever, or any vomiting?
[SEG0019] person_3 (CAREGIVER): No fever. No vomiting. She's still running around at school.
[SEG0020] person_1 (DOCTOR): What about pain, cramps in the tummy?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): A bit. Low down. I don't know, doctor. Not lots.

[SEG0022] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Ja, low tummy, just before she goes, and it eases once she's been. We give buscopan syrup if it's bad, five ml. We did try imodiam one time, from the chemist, and I stopped it the same day. Not for a six year old.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): Is she on anything else, even now and then?
[SEG0024] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Panado syrup, 5 ml, if a headache shows up. Not often. And the purple inhaler for her wheeze. Err, I don't know the proper name, doctor.
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): The purple one is yuck.
[SEG0026] person_3 (CAREGIVER): The sister said two puffs twice a day. She fights me, so most days it never happens. There was also a script for lacteeze and we never gave it. Not once.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any allergies to medicine or food? Rash, swelling, that kind of thing?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0029] person_3 (CAREGIVER): No. Nothing. Her card says no allergies.
[SEG0030] person_1 (DOCTOR): And family, any coeliac disease, or other people who battle with milk?
[SEG0031] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Her brother was told lactose intolerance, years back. No coeliac in the family, not that anyone's said.
[SEG0032] person_1 (DOCTOR): May I feel your tummy? I'll be gentle. Soft, a little bloated, bowel sounds are normal, I can't feel a mass, and she's not tender.
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): Is it bad? I don't know, doctor.

[SEG0034] person_1 (DOCTOR): Shame, I don't think it's something awful. My working idea is lactose intolerance, from the milk and the ice cream. I still want to rule out coeliac, because months of loose stools can be that as well.

[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): Thursday morning the sister takes coeliac bloods, half past eight, at the lab downstairs. Don't fast her, and keep the bread and normal gluten going till then, or the test can't see it. If those bloods come back borderline, then we do the endomysial antibody, a third test. Only if they're borderline.

[SEG0036] person_1 (DOCTOR): Keep a little diet diary for me, food and what the tummy does, till we meet. Stay off milk and ice cream for now. I'll see you in two weeks with the results. If it does not settle once the dairy is out, then we book an abdominal ultrasound.

spec.situation: Person with bloating and loose stools after milk and ice cream for months, no weight loss; tried to avoid dairy for a week; blood test for coeliac planned; diet diary asked.

traps.happens: In the plan the doctor books some tests or visits for a definite time ('the nurse takes bloods Thursday morning', 'I'll see you in two weeks') and makes others conditional ('if those are borderline we do the third test', 'if it does not settle, a scan').
traps.label_rule: Booked or arranged = status planned. Only the hedged ones are conditional. Never mark a booked test conditional or 'if needed'. Instructions for the booked test (fasting, time, medicine timing) belong to that test's action, not a separate invented plan item.

features: colloquial_drug_names: medicines referred to by colour, purpose or brand ('the water tablet', 'Crocin', 'my sugar tablets', 'the purple inhaler'); the name is recorded as said, the normalized name only if it is clear.

stopped_or_never_taken: a medicine the patient stopped, was never given or only took once ('I stopped it in March'). Status discontinued, not current; a medicine never taken is not recorded as a medication.

bad.reason: Dose/frequency and wheeze stated, but current use is doubtful: most days it never happens.
bad.text: purple inhaler (dose=2 puffs, frequency=twice a day, indication=wheeze, status=currently_used, reported_by=caregiver)

omissions.text: Loose stools are not all day; occur 2–3 times/day when loose.
A one-week dairy exclusion (no milk, ice cream, yoghurt) led to marked improvement in bloating; symptoms recurred immediately after a milkshake.
Abdominal pain is crampy/just before stooling and eases after she has been.
Loperamide/Imodium was tried only once, obtained from the chemist, and stopped the same day.
Purple inhaler adherence detail: prescribed two puffs twice a day, but most days it never happens because she resists it.
There was a prescription for Lacteeze/lactase, but it was never given at all.
